lead.tldr: Security: North Korean hack shows multisig social engineering vulnerability, expect heightened scrutiny of non‑custodial platforms. • Quantum research indicates ECC may be broken sooner, prompting urgent migration to post‑quantum curves. • Circle's cirBTC launch offers institutional Bitcoin exposure, but centralization risk may deter DeFi purists. • x402 Foundation partnership positions stablecoin payments for AI agents, potential $5 trillion market by 2030. • Ethereum Foundation nearing staking target reduces ETH sales, generating up to $5.4 million annual yield. • Bitcoin ETF inflows hint at early recovery, countering Q1 outflows and market weakness.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today’s headlines span a massive Drift Protocol hack exposing security gaps, Circle’s launch of institutional‑grade wrapped Bitcoin, and looming mega‑IPOs from SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic that will test retail appetite. Meanwhile, Ethereum’s staking surge and AI‑driven payment standards signal fresh growth avenues.

top_signals.title: North Korea behind $286m Drift Protocol hack, investigators say
top_signals.summary: Investigators attribute the $286 million theft from Drift Protocol to a North Korean‑linked hacking group. The attack on the Solana‑based non‑custodial platform used social engineering of multisignature signers and private‑key compromise, mirroring tactics seen in the Bybit hack. The breach has heightened institutional concerns about DeFi security and drawn criticism of stablecoin issuer Circle for a slow response.

top_signals.title: Weekly Top Stories: Drift drained for $285m
top_signals.summary: The Drift protocol suffered a hack that erased about $285 million from its treasury. The incident underscores operational risk in DeFi platforms that institutional investors monitor closely. In parallel, a joint paper by researchers from Google Quantum AI, Stanford, UC Berkeley and the Ethereum Foundation argued that quantum computers may be capable of breaking elliptic‑curve cryptography much sooner than previously projected. The same briefing noted a Trump administration proposal that would allow crypto assets to be held in U.S. 401(k) retirement plans, a development that could broaden institutional exposure to digital assets.

top_signals.title: Mega-IPOs From SpaceX, OpenAI & Anthropic Will Test Retail Investor Faith
top_signals.summary: Upcoming IPOs of SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic represent some of the largest public offerings in the technology sector. SpaceX intends to raise $75 billion and has committed to allocating roughly one third of its shares to retail investors. The other two companies are also targeting high‑profile listings that will draw significant attention from both institutional and retail markets. Market participants are watching how retail sentiment and a broader down market could influence pricing and allocation decisions for these mega‑IPOs.

top_signals.title: Circle announces plans to debut wrapped Bitcoin for institutions. Here’s what it means
top_signals.summary: Circle has introduced cirBTC, a wrapped token that is fully backed by Bitcoin on a 1:1 basis and is targeted at institutional investors. The token will initially be issued on the Ethereum and Arc blockchains and Circle has outlined a multichain roadmap to extend its availability. By providing a regulated Bitcoin‑linked asset, Circle aims to meet growing institutional demand for Bitcoin liquidity in decentralized finance, though the design also raises questions about centralization of the token’s custody.

top_signals.title: Why Coinbase’s team-up with Amazon, Google and Stripe can turbo-charge AI agents
top_signals.summary: Coinbase has joined the newly created x402 Foundation, which is governed by the Linux Foundation and includes tech giants Amazon, Google and Microsoft/Stripe. The foundation is developing the x402 protocol as a universal standard for embedding stablecoin payments directly into web interactions. This protocol is designed to allow AI agents to execute autonomous transactions using stablecoins. Venture capitalists view the initiative as a catalyst for AI driven payments and project a $5 trillion market by 2030.

top_signals.title: Ethereum Foundation stakes $93 million of ether in a day, reaching its 70,000 ETH target
top_signals.summary: The Ethereum Foundation, the nonprofit organization that oversees the Ethereum protocol, has increased its ETH stake to support network security and generate revenue. A single deposit of $93 million worth of ether raised its total staked holdings to roughly $143 million, bringing it close to its target of 70,000 ETH. By shifting from selling ETH to fund operations toward earning an estimated $3.9 to $5.4 million per year in staking yield, the foundation is creating a sustainable funding source for development and ecosystem initiatives.

top_signals.title: Q1 was bad for crypto, but industry say things are looking up
top_signals.summary: The crypto market contracted by more than 20% in the first quarter, with Bitcoin and Ethereum exchange‑traded funds experiencing a combined $1.2 billion of outflows. Despite the downturn, institutional investors are starting to redeploy capital into the sector. Recent inflows into Bitcoin ETFs are being interpreted as an early sign of a market rebound. The trajectory of the recovery will depend on broader macroeconomic variables such as geopolitical tensions and Federal Reserve policy.

top_signals.title: Dunamu x Naver Financial: Merger Delayed
top_signals.summary: The Korea Fair Trade Commission has extended its review of the planned share exchange between Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, and Naver Financial, pushing the expected closing from June to September. The Financial Supervisory Service also issued a correction order on Dunamu’s disclosure related to the transaction. The merger, valued at roughly KRW 20 trillion (about $13.7 billion), is designed to integrate a cryptocurrency exchange, payments platform and artificial‑intelligence capabilities. Regulators and investors see the combined entity as a potential catalyst for the development of stablecoins and real‑world‑asset tokenization in South Korea.

top_signals.title: 두나무·네이버 합병 지연, 과연 누구를 위한 것인가?
top_signals.summary: The Korean Fair Trade Commission has extended its antitrust review of the planned stock‑swap merger between Dunamu, the operator of the Upbit exchange, and Naver Financial. The Financial Supervisory Service also issued a correction order to Dunamu, prompting the parties to move the expected closing from June to September. Valued at roughly 20 trillion KRW, the transaction is intended to combine exchange, payment and artificial‑intelligence capabilities to launch a stablecoin and real‑world‑asset tokenisation platform. Institutional investors now face heightened regulatory uncertainty that could affect the timing and commercial upside of the combined entity.
